summary: Tier0 restart_core no longer stops itself or the non-supervisor processes it runs under (bootstrap shell, soak watchdog, deploy): the supervisors and their other descendants are still stopped children first, the relaunch always happens even when a lock wait times out, and every boundary leaves a restart_core line (stopped / spared counts) in the boot log.
reason: S24 04/11 12:53: right after Tier0 activated release 20261104T125241, the supervisors were stopped with SIGKILL (Termux tab: Process completed (signal 9)), the deploy of d8e08d9b ended without a receipt and the device stayed offline. The boundary computes every descendant of the supervisors, including its own planner and the shell that must relaunch: when it is requested from inside the supervisor tree (the soak watchdog rollback Popen()s it, and the watchdog is a child of the guardian), it kills itself before the relaunch; under set -e a lock wait timeout also skipped the relaunch.

tests.evidence: 19 tests. New: the real restart_core planner (read from tier0-bootstrap.sh, nothing listed or signalled) spares the watchdog-rollback chain and a deploy chain inside the tree but never a supervisor ancestor, still stops every supervisor descendant children first when requested from outside, and the relaunch is reached after a lock timeout. The previous planner targets the shell and the planner itself in the first case. Already registered in ci.yml.

tests.name: tier0-bootstrap.sh --restart-core (bash, temporary HOME, planner stubbed)
tests.evidence: The heredoc reaches python unchanged and compiles; both lock waits time out without lock files and the script still reaches the relaunch with rc=0; boot.log gets event=restart_core and two event=restart_core_lock_timeout lines.

architecture.reason: Same restart boundary owner (tier0-bootstrap.sh) and same relaunch; only the target set, the timeout path and one boot.log line change. No new process, store or scheduler.

evidence: The Claw bridge depends on the supervisors the boundary relaunches; a boundary that kills its own relaunch leaves the device offline until a human acts.

limitations: The 12:53 sequence is not yet proven from S24 evidence (device offline): the planner killing its own chain is proven for the watchdog rollback path; for the activation path it depends on whether the deploy ran inside the supervisor tree, and an Android kill (phantom process killer or memory pressure, ADB and Wi-Fi off) remains possible. The new boot.log line separates the two next time.
The Tier0 copy of tier0-bootstrap.sh changes only when install-tier0-control.py runs (deploy).
